clock.basis: Unmeasured compact-scene allowances: retain the earlier separate RGB 25-35 min, LWIR 25-35 min and LiDAR 20-30 min ranges; retain 35-45 min physical setup/control and allow 5-10 min essential field checks. Do not silently shorten capture to make a denser schedule fit.
clock.included: Inter-target transfers, parking/access and equipment carry, physical sensor setup and control/checkpoints, RGB/LWIR/LiDAR capture, essential on-site safety and completeness checks, and any breaks occurring during the route.
clock.offline_excluded: Office planning, permit applications, prior equipment preparation and calibration that can be completed off-site, routine data copying/backup that can be done off-site, processing, registration, detailed QA, reconstruction and dataset packaging.
clock.rule: Stop at eight hours. Capture/setup bounds exclude walking and driving; unknown transfer or carry time is never zero. Start another target only if its field work and safe exit fit the remaining time. Four-target groups are ambitious conditional targets, not verified eight-hour days.

summary: Six denser route groups with three or four new targets each, not a guaranteed six-day completion forecast. Eight-hour field-time cap. A fourth target is conditional; defer unfinished work rather than exceed the cap or omit essential field control. No commute to the first target or from the final target is assumed. Between-group target-to-target links are assigned to the following group so no transfer disappears from the sequence; they do not prescribe overnight accommodation or the crew's actual morning origin. Ordering uses a multi-start nearest-neighbour and 2-opt geographic-distance heuristic from target #49. It screens backtracking, not road travel, legal access or a proven global optimum. Preserve modelled road evidence only for matching directed endpoint pairs; all other links stay explicitly schematic. More targets per group do not establish that the group fits eight hours. Geographic sequence length changes from 71.2 to 40.8 km; these are straight-line comparisons, NOT driving distances.
